headline: Highest risk is data leakage from Whisper’s audio-file handling into Dagster workflows; prompt injection and capability conflict are otherwise limited by both profiles’ no-network, no-write defaults.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dagster has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, filesystem read, or MCP surfaces, and Whisper likewise has no clipboard or stdin/stdout surface. With no shared communication channel or parser bridge in either profile, a prompt-injection pathway is not plausible from the documented defaults.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies Whisper text into Dagster as trusted instructions, the risk changes.
IF either agent is wrapped with a shared clipboard or message queue, reassess for injection.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected from shared clipboard workflows.
Do not pipe model text directly into Dagster task definitions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to any inter-agent handoff.
requires-engineering: sanitize and schema-validate all text passed between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dagster touches no data classes and has no filesystem read or network egress, while Whisper touches audio/speech and can consume audio files. The pair does not show a shared workspace or outbound transmission path, so leakage is limited unless an operator places sensitive audio in a shared location.
conditions: IF both agents are given the same directory containing sensitive audio files, leakage risk increases.
IF Whisper outputs transcripts into a shared workspace that Dagster later publishes, data exposure becomes possible.
mitigations: Store audio inputs in a separate folder from Dagster assets.
Delete or redact sensitive audio before transcription.
Restrict transcript exports to approved destinations only.
requires-engineering: add per-file access controls between the agents.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both profiles explicitly lack filesystem write, git modification, subprocess spawning, and network egress. Dagster and Whisper therefore have no overlapping mutable write surface in the documented profiles, so direct capability conflict is provably blocked.
conditions: IF either profile is extended with shared write access, reassess for conflicts.
IF an external wrapper grants both agents the same mutable directory, conflict risk changes.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in deployment.
Avoid granting shared write access to any workspace.
requires-engineering: enforce OS-level sandboxing for mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dagster is a data orchestrator, so its outputs can become downstream inputs, while Whisper produces transcripts from audio files. If Dagster treats Whisper output as authoritative without verification, transcription errors can cascade into pipelines in default-style orchestration flows, though the profiles do not prove an automatic handoff.
conditions: IF Dagster consumes Whisper transcripts without human or schema verification, cascading errors occur.
IF Whisper is used to generate labels or facts that Dagster schedules automatically, downstream mistakes propagate.
mitigations: Add a verification step before Dagster consumes transcripts.
Require schema checks on Whisper outputs.
Sample-check a small batch of transcripts before automation.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and human review gates.

E_compliance.rationale: Dagster’s profile shows no data classes touched, while Whisper explicitly touches audio and speech. No residency, retention, or certification mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to ordinary handling of audio content rather than a proven policy conflict between the two agents.
conditions: IF audio inputs contain regulated content and are routed to a noncompliant storage location, compliance risk increases.
IF retention policies differ between transcript storage and audio storage, reassess.
mitigations: Apply the same retention policy to audio and transcripts.
Delete temporary audio artifacts after use.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls for both agents.
